problems: The Cliopatria row 'Kingdom of Georgia' (1010..1802) is three states. kingdom-of-georgia (1008-1478) reviews shapes 1010..1462 and 1468; its verdict wrong on shapes 1507..1578 and 1706..1762 hands them to kingdom-of-kartli (whose dossier already re-uses them from 1478), and its verdict wrong on 1763..1802 hands them to the new kingdom-of-kartli-kakheti.

kingdom-of-kartli and kingdom-of-kakheti name kingdom-of-georgia as their 1762 successor; it should be kingdom-of-kartli-kakheti. The Kartli dossier starts in 1478, so 1463-1477 is covered only by the new keyframes kingdom-of-georgia_1463 and the 1468 shape.

kingdom-of-georgia ends in 1478 (tripartite division, Kartli page) although the kingdom's page says 1463 de facto / 1490 de jure and kingdom-of-imereti founds in 1463; chosen so Kartli takes over without a gap.

A new keyframe whose years lie inside a Cliopatria shape (kingdom-of-georgia_1010b, _1130, _1422b) overrides that shape in those years; the shape's own verdict says which years it stands for. Renderers must honour this.

kingdom-of-kartli-kakheti lists the Name 'Kingdom of Georgia' in cliopatria_names, so the validator prints 34 'no verdict' warnings for shapes reviewed in kingdom-of-georgia; expected for a split, 0 errors. kingdom-of-georgia has 4 warnings for counterpart slugs without dossiers (kingdom-of-kakheti-hereti, kingdom-of-tashir-dzoraget).

Vassal tints belong to the suzerain's dossier: russian-empire (vassal_start 1783-07 to vassal_end 1801-09, counterpart kingdom-of-kartli-kakheti), mongol-empire / ilkhanate (Georgia a vassal from 1243), timurid-empire (1395-1406, counterpart kingdom-of-georgia), safavid-dynasty and ottoman-empire for Kartli.
byzantine-empire (eu-05) must carry Vaspurakan from 1022 (Cliopatria draws kingdom-of-vaspurakan to 1027) and Tao, Javakheti etc. in 1023.
kingdom-of-kartli-kakheti.wikidata is null (Wikidata unreachable). The Georgia dossier has no ruler strip.

WebFetch answers come from a small summariser model: every quote was taken from the fragments it returned, and dates it inferred from link titles or context were not used as page dates (flagged in notes). The Basil II page, read for the Vaspurakan cession, is cited only in kingdom-of-vaspurakan.
